verses.text: Peter and John were going up into the temple at the hour of prayer, the ninth hour.

A certain man who was lame from his mother’s womb was being carried, whom they laid daily at the door of the temple which is called Beautiful, to ask gifts for the needy of those who entered into the temple.
Seeing Peter and John about to go into the temple, he asked to receive gifts for the needy.
Peter, fastening his eyes on him, with John, said, “Look at us.”
He listened to them, expecting to receive something from them.
But Peter said, “I have no silver or gold, but what I have, that I give you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, get up and walk!”
He took him by the right hand, and raised him up. Immediately his feet and his ankle bones received strength.
Leaping up, he stood, and began to walk. He entered with them into the temple, walking, leaping, and praising God.
All the people saw him walking and praising God.
They recognized him, that it was he who used to sit begging for gifts for the needy at the Beautiful Gate of the temple. They were filled with wonder and amazement at what had happened to him.
As the lame man who was healed held on to Peter and John, all the people ran together to them in the porch that is called Solomon’s, greatly wondering.
When Peter saw it, he responded to the people, “You men of Israel, why do you marvel at this man? Why do you fasten your eyes on us, as though by our own power or godliness we had made him walk?
The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the God of our fathers, has glorified his Servant Jesus, whom you delivered up, and denied in the presence of Pilate, when he had determined to release him.
But you denied the Holy and Righteous One, and asked for a murderer to be granted to you,
and killed the Prince of life, whom God raised from the dead, to which we are witnesses.
By faith in his name, his name has made this man strong, whom you see and know. Yes, the faith which is through him has given him this perfect soundness in the presence of you all.
“Now, brothers,  I know that you did this in ignorance, as did also your rulers.
But the things which God announced by the mouth of all his prophets, that Christ should suffer, he thus fulfilled.
“Repent therefore, and turn again, that your sins may be blotted out, so that there may come times of refreshing from the presence of the Lord,
and that he may send Christ Jesus, who was ordained for you before,
whom heaven must receive until the times of restoration of all things, which God spoke long ago by the mouth of his holy prophets.
For Moses indeed said to the fathers, ‘The Lord God will raise up a prophet for you from among your brothers, like me. You shall listen to him in all things whatever he says to you.
It will be that every soul that will not listen to that prophet will be utterly destroyed from among the people.’
Yes, and all the prophets from Samuel and those who followed after, as many as have spoken, they also told of these days.
You are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying to Abraham, ‘In your offspring  will all the families of the earth be blessed.’
God, having raised up his servant Jesus, sent him to you first to bless you, in turning away every one of you from your wickedness.”

footnotes.content: Peter and John were heading to prayer—such ordinary faith, such holy habit. They were going *up*, which is how we live when Christ lives in us: toward the presence of the Father.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Crippled from birth, carried daily to the Beautiful Gate—that is, placed at the threshold of beauty while he himself could not walk there. How often we wait at the gates of grace, not knowing we stand at the very door of our healing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He asked them for alms, expecting coins. He could not have imagined what Peter's eyes held for him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Look at us"—a piercing command wrapped in invitation. Jesus often asked people to *see*, as though the first healing must happen in the eyes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He listened, his hope quickening. We are most open to the Lord when we have given up and are simply waiting.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Peter's honesty: "I have no silver or gold." But what a treasure he held—the name of Jesus Christ. In that name, all sufficiency. Sometimes the most powerful gifts come when we surrender what we do not have and offer what we do.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Peter *took him by the right hand and raised him up*—an act of full identification. Jesus does not heal from a distance; He touches, He lifts, He draws near. And immediately, strength flooded those broken ankles.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Leaping, standing, walking, praising—joy exploded out of him. The Lord's healing is never quiet; it spills over into praise, into movement, into witness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All the people *saw him*—the whole temple knew this man, crippled for decades, now whole. There is no healing without witness; the Lord's work invites the world to see.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They recognized him—this was no stranger, no distant wonder. His neighbors watched his own transformation in real time, which is where faith begins: not in rumor, but in the changed life we know.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The healed man held on to Peter and John in Solomon's Porch—wonder drawing people together around those who had been touched by the Lord. A porch becomes a pulpit when witnesses gather.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Peter redirected their gaze at once: "Why are you marveling at *us*?" The apostle's humility is like a mirror—he turns it away from himself and toward the One who acted. This is the posture of a true servant.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He spoke of God glorifying His *Servant* Jesus—a name rooted in Isaiah's Suffering Servant. Peter sees the Resurrection as God's vindication of a rejected, crucified Man. The Cross was not the end; it was the means.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "The Holy and Righteous One"—Peter names what Jesus *was* at the moment they chose a murderer instead. Our refusal of Christ is always a refusal of holiness, of righteousness, of His nature itself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You killed the Prince of life—a paradox that stings. They silenced the One from whom all breath comes. Yet God raised Him from the dead, and Peter stands there as *witness*, declaring what his eyes have seen.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: By faith in His name, His name made this man strong. The healing proves the power of Jesus' name—not as magic, but as the efficacy of His Person working through trust. Faith is not belief in a doctrine; it is believing *in Him*.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Peter speaks a hard word wrapped in gentleness: "You did this in ignorance." Even as he confronts them, he extends mercy. He knows what grace can do even to those who crucified the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: What God announced, Christ fulfilled. Peter shows them that the *suffering* of Jesus was not a mistake or a tragedy—it was prophecy coming true, the very work of God unfolding as it was foretold.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Repent and turn again, that your sins may be blotted out." Peter holds out the possibility of erasure itself—as though the Lord's mercy is so complete that He can wipe away the very record of our turning away. And refreshing shall come.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He may send Christ Jesus, ordained for you before. Peter speaks of the Ascended Christ who is *ready*, held in heaven, prepared to be sent in blessing to those who turn to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Heaven must receive Him until the times of restoration—all things renewed, all things restored. This is not the end of the story; it is a pause. The Lord waits in heaven for the day when creation itself is made whole again.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Peter quotes Moses promising a Prophet like him—a voice that echoes through all of Scripture. Jesus is that Prophet, the One to whom all the law and prophets point, and to whom we must listen.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Every soul that will not listen to Him shall be destroyed. There is urgency here, but also clarity: the only way to life is to listen to Jesus. In this there is both warning and invitation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All the prophets from Samuel onward spoke of these days—the days unfolding before Peter's hearers. We live *inside* the fulfillment; the Lord is completing what generations longed to see.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You are the children of the prophets and of the covenant. Peter reminds them that they inherit a promise made to Abraham himself—that through his offspring, all families would be blessed. Jesus is that blessing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God raised up Jesus and sent Him to you first, to bless you by turning each of you from wickedness. Readers today hear an echo in these words: the Lord still sends Jesus to us, still comes to bless us by undoing our rebellion. He always comes first to offer grace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
